first_panel.note: Three seats each rated the first draft 3 of 5 and found one high-severity issue. All three were fixed, and this review found each resolved. Its medium and low notes that were not fixed with them are superseded by this review's list, which was made on the patched page.

issues.issue: The quote is cut so the disclaimer reads as covering the whole legal classification. P-078 says the witness has no opinion on whether the cited contract terms, 'standing alone,' resolve any legal classification. Card 6 (line 208) states it correctly; card 1 states it more broadly and weakens the petitioners' evidence.
issues.fix: The PSC staff's witness said 'I am not a lawyer and do not have an opinion as to whether, standing alone, they resolve any legal classification under Georgia law,' about the contract language the witness cited. [P-078]

issues.issue: Card 1 puts the staff witness's per-kWh sentence under 'What supports it' but leaves VoltaGrid's direct answer on how Serverfarm pays (same passage, P-046) out of the card. A reader of card 1 alone sees one side's fee evidence and not the other's.
issues.fix: Add after the quote: VoltaGrid's executive also said Serverfarm pays 'in amounts based on the Conversion Assets' producing capacity in operation, rather than a fee per kWh of energy that the Conversion Assets actually deliver.' [P-046]

issues.issue: The page's own voice describes the deal as 'turning a customer's gas into power for a fee', which is VoltaGrid's account (P-046). The petitioners call it a plan 'to sell power' (P-027). Using one side's description inside the question gives that side the framing.
issues.fix: Whether VoltaGrid's arrangement with Serverfarm, which VoltaGrid describes as converting Serverfarm's gas into electricity for a fee and the petitioners describe as a power sale, is a retail sale of electricity is a legal question the PSC has not decided as of Nov 14, 2026. (Use the same neutral wording at line 214.)
